basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 24:2-3 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 212. [Quaeritur] quid significat quod Abraham puero suo dicit: Pone manum tuam'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 212. [Quaeritur] quid significat quod Abraham puero suo dicit: Pone manum tuam super femur meum, et jura per Dominum Deum coeli (Gen. XXIV, 2, 3)?-- Resp. Tradunt Hebraei quod in sanctificatione ejus, hoc est circumcisione, juraverit. Sed melius intelligendum est jurasse in semine Abrahae, hoc est Christo. Quia ipse Dominus Deus coeli in ea carne tum venturus erat, quae de illo femore propagata est.
